stem:
Two parallel metal plates X and Y are separated by a distance of 0.041 m, as shown in Fig. 6.1.

[[fig:f1]]

There is a vacuum between the plates. An electron is at rest at the centre of plate X.

A potential difference (p.d.) of 58 kV is applied across the plates. This causes the electron to accelerate towards plate Y.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: On Fig. 6.1, use the symbols + and − to indicate which of plates X and Y is the positive plate and which is the negative plate.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the electric field strength *E* between the plates. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the acceleration of the electron.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.lead: Many electrons are now accelerated from rest from plate X to plate Y in Fig. 6.1. When the electrons hit plate Y, the absorption of their kinetic energies results in the emission of electromagnetic waves.
parts.text: Show that the minimum wavelength of these electromagnetic waves is 21 pm.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the region of the electromagnetic spectrum that contains these waves.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Explain how these electromagnetic waves may be used to form images of internal body structures.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.1
figures.alt: Two vertical parallel metal plates X and Y face each other across a 0.041 m gap, with an electron at plate X and the gap labelled vacuum.
